title: Pool_Exhaustion trigger requires the surge class's own drop — pinned contract says ANY pool drop
detail: When the E22 ladder sheds a lower-priority resident (class != surge) to admit the surge — reachable once the player assigns QoS lanes — the pool sits at cap and sheds, yet no crisis fires. The class filter contradicts the pinned "any" definition.
recommended_fix: Use an any-class drop probe for the pool backstop (reason match without the class filter), or amend the frozen root-cause definition to pin the class filter explicitly.

title: surge.dem omits the spec'd mid-run capacity fix — no Crisis_Resolved pin in the golden
detail: The frozen golden spec and design notes pin a mid-run fix plus `Crisis_Resolved` at the exact drain tick, read from the run and pinned in demo comment + tests. The shipped demo never fixes, never resolves, and the golden never pins a resolved event.
recommended_fix: Add the spec'd mid-run wide draw and pin the resolve tick in comments/goldens, or record a spec-changelog entry documenting the deliberate demo redesign.

title: Drop payload growth breaks the frozen 'pre-4.2 streams byte-identical' promise — contract text unamended
detail: Every Packet_Dropped now serializes 4 extra bytes, so pre-4.2 streams containing drops are NOT byte-identical; all drop-bearing T1s shifted beyond the catalog fold. The change log documents the cause, but the frozen promise and the Event comment still claim byte-identity.
recommended_fix: Amend the frozen Events constraint and the types.odin comment to state the drop-payload growth, so the golden-stability contract matches the code.

title: Trigger names the drop's bundle before the slot-order scan — pinned 'a → first hit' order reversed
detail: On a tick with a surge-class drop, the code attributes the crisis to the drop's bundle, which can differ from the slot-order-first saturated bundle the frozen contract pins. Change-log #1 documents the reversal (round-1 KEEP) but the frozen text still states the old order.
recommended_fix: Amend the frozen trigger contract to pin drop-first attribution (the admission-time evidence), matching the round-1 KEEP decision.

title: crisis_record_run makes without an explicit allocator and leaks its events array in the replay test
detail: ODN-18 requires an explicit allocator on every make (the pre-existing record_run takes `allocator := context.allocator`); the replay test discards the events dynamic via `_`, leaking 2x256B per the tracking allocator. The change log's "leak hygiene" claim is incomplete.
recommended_fix: Add an allocator parameter to crisis_record_run and `defer delete` the events array in test_crisis_replay_identity.

title: Crisis engine consumes the ODN-14 event buffer as sim input, making the app's never-drain behavior a correctness contract
detail: Sim logic now reads the cross-layer event buffer whose documented contract is app-side draining after each step. Any future app drain/filter (ODN-14's purpose) silently breaks crisis trigger/resolve attribution; the tripwire comment is a human-only guard.
recommended_fix: Have flow_step record per-tick drop sites in a dedicated per-tick field on Flow_State (cleared each tick); crisis_evaluate reads that instead of scanning state.events.

title: Step tick-monotonicity latch rejects only backward ticks, not repeats, despite claiming strictly monotonic
detail: The documented invariant is strict monotonicity; the check enforces only non-decreasing. A tick == state.tick call would re-execute the whole tick (double spawn, double flow, duplicate events for one tick). No current caller does it, but the guard is weaker than its claim.
recommended_fix: Reject equality too: `if tick <= state.tick` — or amend the comment to document non-decreasing semantics.

title: Stale golden-stability comment in state_writer now contradicts the 4.2 drop-payload growth
detail: The 4.2 line grows every Packet_Dropped payload by 4 bytes, so drop-bearing T1 manifests shift (deliberate, cause-documented re-bless). The adjacent comment still asserts "existing T1 manifests must not shift" with no 4.2 exception — misleading for future maintainers.
recommended_fix: Amend the comment: note the 4.2 drop-payload exception and the cause-documented re-bless, keeping the no-drop-stream byte-identity claim.

title: E13 dedup key (archetype, set_piece) is coarser than arch §6.4's per-root-cause key; comments conflate the two
detail: The (archetype, set_piece) key permits at most one active crisis per activation regardless of kind; §6.4's per-root-cause key would allow distinct simultaneous causes. While a Saturated_Bundle crisis is active, the Pool_Exhaustion backstop for the same set-piece is suppressed until resolve. MVP-safe; comments conflate both keys.
recommended_fix: Key active/cooldown entries on (archetype, set_piece, kind) to match §6.4, or update the §6.4 comment to pin the per-activation key.

title: Trigger root-cause attribution contradicts the frozen pinned definition (drop-first, drop's bundle vs slot-order scan)
detail: The pinned definition selects the first saturated bundle in slot order with the settled scan (a) first; the code evaluates the drop (b) first and names the drop's own bundle, which may differ from the first at-bound bundle. The change log records the deviation but the frozen block was never amended.
recommended_fix: Amend the frozen Trigger-contract block to the implemented drop-first attribution, or restore slot-order selection in crisis_evaluate so the pinned definition holds.

title: Monotonicity latch rejects only backward ticks; equal ticks pass despite the 'strictly monotonic' claim

recommended_fix: On a cooldown block in the drop branch, fall through to the settled scan and pool backstop instead of continuing.

recommended_fix: Key the active row on the stable pair identity (bundle_lo/bundle_hi node ids at trigger) or the stable member pipe id, re-resolving the current slot; add a test demolishing an earlier-ordered pair while the crisis is active.

title: Wrong-typed archetype_id silently treated as absent (fail-open) instead of fail-fast

title: Step tick-latch is non-strict — tick == state.tick re-runs the tick despite the 'strictly monotonic' claim
detail: The guard rejects only backward ticks; a caller passing tick == state.tick proceeds through state.tick = tick and re-runs commands/flow/eval for the same tick without latching replay_error — the 'never silent' latch misses the equality case.
recommended_fix: Change to `if tick <= state.tick { state.replay_error = true; return }` — all callers step from state.tick + 1, so equality is never legitimate.

title: Era set-piece index truncated to u16 with no roster cap (archetypes got a 255 cap for the same reason)

recommended_fix: Cap era set-piece count at load (<= 65535, or 255 for symmetry) with a named error, mirroring the archetype roster cap.

title: The 4.2 step tick-monotonicity latch has zero test coverage

recommended_fix: Add a test stepping tick N then N-1, asserting replay_error latched, state.tick unchanged, and no events appended; mirror the command-failure latch coverage if one is added.
